$comment: Scoop manifest template. The release workflow substitutes 0.5.3,
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.3/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and 9a7e32bc9cabb380fb8a6deed9450df67e6bfa45ac542bce7919e151edb473cc and commits the result to the bucket repository.
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.3/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip is on the public downloads CDN, never a GitHub release: this
repository is private, so a GitHub URL is a 404 for everyone who would
install from a public bucket. There is no `checkver`/`autoupdate` for the
same reason: the release workflow pushes the new manifest itself, and
the GitHub API it would poll is not open to the public either.
9a7e32bc9cabb380fb8a6deed9450df67e6bfa45ac542bce7919e151edb473cc is read from the .sha256 the release publishes beside the
archive, the same one the patched PowerShell installer verifies against,
so there is exactly one published hash per archive.
post_install: Write-Host 'yoink installed. Run `yoink doctor` to check it over.'
